Radius of the circle used for "nearby" pixels, as a proportion of image width or height (whichever is larger). Directly adjacent pixels will always be considered nearby, even if this is set to zero.

Differences in the foreground mask values of these nearby pixels will be extrapolated to estimate RGB of the original foreground and background images.

This should be set to a value:
- large enough to overcome any noise in the original images,
- small enough to capture relevant details in the original images,
- large enough that different foreground mask values can actually be found, if the foreground mask has large flat areas of partial opacity,
- small enough that the operation does not run too slowly.

The types of light path bounce on this object that this rule should apply to.

When a light path hits this object, any ray(s) that bounce off will do so with all applicable trace set visibility rules applied, depending on the type of the bounce.

For example, a rule that only applies to reflection bounces will only affect which objects are visible in reflections on this object.

For shadows, a bounce occurs before choosing a light source (this allows controlling which objects and light sources can cast shadows on this object), and then a fake bounce occurs on the chosen light source before tracing to see whether a shadow is cast (this allows controlling which specific combinations of objects and light sources can cast shadows).

Reflection: specular (and glossy) reflection bounces.
Refraction: specular (and glossy) transmission bounces.
Diffuse: diffuse bounces (reflection and transmission), volume scatter bounces and bounces for tracing dirt, curvature and round edges.
Shadow: direct light bounces, bounces for tracing ambient occlusion, and fake bounces that occur after choosing a light for direct light tracing.

Checks if a cache file can be found for the given geometry import preferences and filename / meshlet ID attribute. If a meshlet cache file exists it will be opened and kept open by the mesh node.

This function can be used before or after the mesh node is evaluated. When you call it before evaluation you don't have to populate the actual geometry attributes yet. This allows you to check whether you need to populate the geometry data or not and thus save a bit of memory and time.

If the meshlet cache file exists and the node was not evaluated yet you still have to evaluate the mesh node to populate the material / object layer names and pins and bring the node into a consistent state.

If the meshlet cache file does not exist you will have to completely populate the geometry attributes and then evaluate the mesh node. This will then kick off the meshlet build in the background. You can check the state of that build using checkMeshletBuildStatus().
Checks the status of the cached meshlet mesh for the given mesh node. This should be run *after* the mesh node got evaluated and any meshlet data was loaded or its build was started.
Deletes the meshlet cache file of the given node if the file isn't used anywhere else. This can be called before or after evaluation of the mesh node.

If set to TRUE the mesh will be converted to a meshlet asset. Meshlets can be used to minimize the amount of mesh data that is being rendered depending on the film resolution and camera view.
The conversion to meshlets starts after the evaluation of the mesh node. The created meshlet data is stored in a file in the meshlet cache.
If the mesh has already been converted to meshlets, the source data will not be loaded. However, A_MATERIAL_NAMES and A_OBJECT_NAMES will still be populated with the name lists stored in the meshlet cache file.
If the mesh is not coming from a file, A_MESHLET_MESH_ID will also need to be set to identify mesh data between sessions. If it's not set, the mesh will not be converted to meshlets.

Gets the file name of the meshlet cache file if the mesh node has an associated meshlet cache file or an empty string if it does not. A meshlet cache file is only assigned to a mesh node if A_CONVERT_TO_MESHLETS is set to true and the mesh node either has been evaluated or hasMeshletCacheFile() has been called with this node.
Deletes all meshlet cache files for a given meshlet mesh ID that are currently not in use anywhere.

The file names of supplementary script assets to be packed into or read from an ORBX archive that this nodegraph requires. When the scene file is loaded from a filesystem, this attribute functions as a setter; when the scene file is loaded from an ORBX package, it functions as a getter. This attribute is cleared when a new scene file is loaded or when the scene is reloaded. Create an entry in the A_ASSET_PACKAGES attribute for each entry added to this attribute. Use an empty string if the file is a standalone file. The array size of the A_ASSET_PACKAGES attribute must match this attribute to avoid undefined behavior.

Package filenames that contain supplementary assets. Create an entry in this attribute for each entry added to the A_ASSET_FILENAMES attribute. Use an empty string if the corresponding entry in the A_ASSET_FILENAMES is a standalone file and not in a ORBX package. The array sizes of the A_ASSET_FILENAMES and A_ASSET_PACKAGES attributes must match to avoid undefined behavior.

Package filenames that contain supplementary assets. Create an entry in this attribute for each entry added to the A_ASSET_FILENAMES attribute. Use an empty string if the corresponding entry in the A_ASSET_FILENAMES is a standalone file and not in a ORBX package. The array sizes of the A_ASSET_FILENAMES and A_ASSET_PACKAGES attributes must match to avoid undefined behavior.\nUse the Helper API functions appendAsset, removeAsset, and getAsset to manage A_ASSET_FILENAMES and A_ASSET_PACKAGES attributes.

The file names of supplementary assets to be packed into or read from a ORBX archive that this nodegraph requires. A module may determine how to handle this attribute, however, the intended usage is to treat it as a setter when the module's functionality is executed outside of a ORBX package, and as a getter when the module's functionality is executed from a package. Create an entry in the A_ASSET_PACKAGES attribute for each entry added to this attribute. Use an empty string if the file is a standalone file. The array size of the A_ASSET_PACKAGES attribute must match this attribute to avoid undefined behavior.\nUse the Helper API functions appendAsset, removeAsset, and getAsset to manage A_ASSET_FILENAMES and A_ASSET_PACKAGES attributes.
The package containing the module scripts. This is an internal attribute. Octane automatically manages this attribute along with corresponding A_REQUIRED_LUA_FILENAMES attribute.

The file names of the Lua modules required to run the script. This is an internal attribute. Octane automatically identifies modules added using the Lua require command in the script and adds them to this attribute.

Package filenames that contain supplementary assets. Create an entry in this attribute for each entry added to the A_ASSET_FILENAMES attribute. Use an empty string if the corresponding entry in the A_ASSET_FILENAMES is a standalone file and not in a ORBX package. The array sizes of the A_ASSET_FILENAMES and A_ASSET_PACKAGES attributes must match to avoid undefined behavior.\nUse the Helper API functions appendAsset, removeAsset, and getAsset to manage A_ASSET_FILENAMES and A_ASSET_PACKAGES attributes.

The file names of supplementary script assets to be packed into or read from a ORBX archive that this script graph requires. The intended usage is to treat it as a setter when the script is executed from the filesystem, and as a getter when the script is executed from a ORBX package. This attribute is cleared when a new script is loaded or when the script is reloaded. Create an entry in the A_ASSET_PACKAGES attribute for each entry added to this attribute. Use an empty string if the file is a standalone file. The array size of the A_ASSET_PACKAGES attribute must match this attribute to avoid undefined behavior.
Use the Helper API functions appendAsset, removeAsset, and getAsset to manage A_ASSET_FILENAMES and A_ASSET_PACKAGES attributes.

LUA example 
--Check whether the script is running from a package or from disk
local package = graph:getAttribute(octane.A_PACKAGE)
 if package == then
 --Script is running from disk
 local filePath = <pathToFile>
 self : appendAsset(filePath)
else
 --Script is running from a ORBX package
 local filePath = self:getAsset()
end

local handle = octane.file.fopen(filePath)

A tile grid image is an image split into multiple tiles on a regular grid. The entire image is mapped onto one UV unit square, in the same way as regular image texture nodes. All tiles must have the same size, except for tiles along the borders, which may be more narrow.
The most recent choice of whether to use an OCIO color space when exporting AOVs in a nonlinear format such as PNG.
The most recent color space chosen when exporting AOVs in a linear format such as EXR.
The most recent premultiplied alpha setting chosen when exporting render passes in a format that supports choosing premultiplied alpha.
The anisotropy of the specular and transmissive material, 1 is full anisotropy, 0 is isotropy.
The anisotropy of the coating layer, 1 is full anisotropy, 0 is isotropy.

MaterialX Separate 2 channels node: Split the channels of a 2-channel stream into separate float outputs.
MaterialX Separate 3 channels node: Split the channels of a 3-channel stream into separate float outputs.
MaterialX Separate 4 channels node: Split the channels of a 4-channel stream into separate float outputs.

MaterialX Ambient Occlusion global node: Compute the ambient occlusion at the shaded surface point, returning a scalar value between 0 and 1. Ambient occlusion represents the accessibility of each surface point to ambient lighting, with larger values representing greater accessibility to light.

MaterialX Image node: Samples data from a single image, or from a layer within a multi-layer image. When used in the context of rendering a geometry, the image is mapped onto the geometry based on geometry UV coordinates.
MaterialX Tiled Image node: Samples data from a single image, with provisions for tiling and offsetting the image across uv space.
MaterialX Hex Tiled image node: Samples data from a single image, with provisions for hex-tiling and randomizing the image across UV space without an obvious repeating pattern.
MaterialX Hex Tiled Normal Map image node: Samples data from a single normal map image, with provisions for hex-tiling and randomizing the image across UV space without an obvious repeating pattern.
MaterialX LatLong image node: Samples an equiangular (latitude/longitude) image along a view direction with adjustable latitudinal offset.

MaterialX Switch conditional node: Output the value of one of up to 10 inputs, according to the value of a selector input 'which'. Note that not all inputs need to be connected. The output has the same type as 'in1', with a default value of 0.
MaterialX If Greater conditional node: Output the value of the 'in1' or 'in2' input depending on whether the 'value1' input is greater than the 'value2' input.
MaterialX If Greater or Equal conditional node: Output the value of the 'in1' or 'in2' input depending on whether the 'value1' input is greater than or equal to the 'value2' input.
MaterialX If Equal conditional node: Output the value of the 'in1' or 'in2' input depending on whether the 'value1' input is equal to the 'value2' input.
MaterialX If Equal (Boolean Input) conditional node: Output the value of the 'in1' or 'in2' input depending on whether the 'value1' input is equal to the 'value2' input.
MaterialX If Greater (Boolean Output) conditional node: Output a boolean value of 'true' or 'false' depending on whether the 'value1' input is greater than the 'value2' input.
MaterialX If Greater or Equal (Boolean Output) conditional node: Output a boolean value of 'true' or 'false' depending on whether the 'value1' input is greater than or equal to the 'value2' input.
MaterialX If Equal (Boolean Output) conditional node: Output a boolean value of 'true' or 'false' depending on whether the 'value1' input is equal to the 'value2' input.
MaterialX Not logical node: Output a boolean value of 'true' if the 'in' input is 'false', and output the value of 'false' if the 'in' input is 'true'.
MaterialX And logical node: Output a boolean value of 'true' if both 'in1' and 'in2' inputs are 'true', otherwise outputs a boolean value of 'false'.
MaterialX Or logical node: Output a boolean value of 'true' if either or both of the 'in1' and 'in2' inputs are 'true', otherwise outputs a boolean value of 'false'.
MaterialX Xor logical node: Output a boolean value of 'true' if one of the 'in1' or 'in2' inputs is 'true' but not the other, otherwise outputs a boolean value of 'false'.
MaterialX Contrast adjustment node: Increase or decrease the contrast of the 'in' input using the 'amount' input as a linear slope multiplier.
MaterialX Smooth Step adjustment node: Output a smooth, hermite-interpolated remapping of input values from ['low', 'high'] to [0,1].
MaterialX Remap adjustment node: Linearly remap incoming values from one range of values ['inlow', 'inhigh'] to another ['outlow', 'outhigh'].

MaterialX Range adjustment node: Remap incoming values from one range of values to another, optionally applying a gamma correction 'in the middle'. Input values below the 'inlow' input or above the 'outhigh' are extrapolated, unless 'doclamp' is 'true'.
MaterialX Color Correct adjustment node: Combines various adjustment nodes into one artist-friendly color correction node (alpha channel is left unchanged if present).

MaterialX HSV adjustment node: Adjust the hue, saturation and value of an RGB color by converting the input color to HSV, adding amount.x to the hue, multiplying the saturation by amount.y, multiplying the value by amount.z, then converting back to RGB. A positive amount.x rotates hue in the 'red to green to blue' direction, with 'amount' of 1.0 being the equivalent to a 360 degree (e.g. no-op) rotation. Negative or greater-than-1.0 hue adjustment values are allowed, wrapping at the 0-1 boundaries (alpha channel is left unchanged if present).

MaterialX HSV to RGB adjustment node: Convert an incoming color from HSV to RGB space (with H and S ranging from 0 to 1). This conversion is not affected by the current color space and alpha channel is left unchanged if present.

MaterialX RGB to HSV adjustment node: Convert an incoming color from RGB to HSV space (with H and S ranging from 0 to 1). This conversion is not affected by the current color space and alpha channel is left unchanged if present.
MaterialX Luminance adjustment node: Output a grayscale value containing the luminance of the incoming RGB color in all color channels (alpha channel is left unchanged if present).

MaterialX Saturate adjustment node: Adjust the saturation of a color (alpha channel is left unchanged if present). Note that this operation is not equivalent to the 'amount.y' saturation adjustment of 'hsvadjust', as that operator does not account for colorspace.

MaterialX Plus blend compositing node: Add the 'bg' input to the 'fg' input, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The math for Alpha is the same as for R or RGB.

MaterialX Minus blend compositing node: Subtracts the 'bg' input from the 'fg' input, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The math for Alpha is the same as for R or RGB.

MaterialX Difference blend compositing node: Outputs the absolute difference between the 'bg' and 'fg' inputs, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The math for Alpha is the same as for R or RGB.

MaterialX Burn blend compositing node: Darkens the 'fg' input using the 'bg' input, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The math for Alpha is the same as for R or RGB.

MaterialX Dodge blend compositing node: Lightens the 'fg' input using the 'bg' input, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The math for Alpha is the same as for R or RGB.

MaterialX Screen blend compositing node: Inverts the 'fg' and 'bg' inputs, multiplies them together, and then inverts the result, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The math for Alpha is the same as for R or RGB.

MaterialX Overlay blend compositing node: Overlays the 'fg' input over the 'bg' input, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The math for Alpha is the same as for R or RGB.

MaterialX Disjoint-Over merge compositing node: Combines the 'fg' and 'bg' RGBA inputs depending on if the combined alpha of 'fg' and 'bg' are 1 or less, or greater than 1, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The alpha channel of the RGBA inputs is used to control how they are combined.

MaterialX In merge compositing node: Merges the 'fg' and 'bg' RGBA inputs such that only 'fg' values that are in the 'bg' alpha are preserved, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The alpha channel of the RGBA inputs is used to control how they are combined.

MaterialX Out merge compositing node: Merges the 'fg' and 'bg' RGBA inputs such that only 'fg' values that are not in the 'bg' alpha are preserved, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The alpha channel of the RGBA inputs is used to control how they are combined.

MaterialX Over merge compositing node: Merges the 'fg' and 'bg' RGBA inputs such that only 'bg' values that are not in the 'fg' alpha are preserved, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The alpha channel of the RGBA inputs is used to control how they are combined.

MaterialX Mask merge compositing node: Merges the 'fg' and 'bg' RGBA inputs such that only 'bg' values that are in the 'fg' alpha are preserved, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The alpha channel of the RGBA inputs is used to control how they are combined.

MaterialX Matte merge compositing node: Merges the 'fg' and 'bg' RGBA inputs such that only the 'fb' values that are in the 'fg' alpha and 'bg' values that are not in the 'fg' alpha are preserved, optionally blending the original 'bg' (where 'mix' is 0) with the result of the operation (where 'mix' is 1). The alpha channel of the RGBA inputs is used to control how they are combined.
MaterialX Premult alpha node: Multiplies the RGB channels of the input by the Alpha channel of the input.
MaterialX Un-Premult alpha node: Divide the RGB channels of the input by the Alpha channel of the input. If the Alpha value is zero, the original RGBA input value is passed through unchanged.
MaterialX Inside mask compositing node: Masks the 'in' input by multiplying it with the 'mask' input.
MaterialX Outside mask compositing node: Masks the 'in' input by multiplying it with the inverse of the 'mask' input, preserving the inputs that are outside of the mask.
MaterialX Mix node: Blends from the 'bg' input to the 'fg' input based on the 'mix' input.
MaterialX Invert math node: Subtract the 'in' input from the 'amount' input in all channels.
MaterialX Absval math node: Computes the per-channel absolute value of the 'in' input.
MaterialX ACos math node: Computes the angle in radians of the arc-cosine of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Add math node: Adds the 'in1' and 'in2' inputs.
MaterialX ASin math node: Computes the angle in radians of the arc-sinus of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Ceil math node: Computes the per-channel nearest integer value greater than or equal to the 'in' input (the output remains in floating point per-channel, i.e. the same type as the input).
MaterialX Cos math node: Computes the cosine of the angle in radians of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Divide math node: Divide the 'in1' input by the 'in2' input. Vector/Color types divide component-wise, while for matrices 'in1' is multiplied by the inverse of 'in2'.
MaterialX Exp math node: Raises the constant 'e' to the power of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Floor math node: Computes the per-channel nearest integer value less than or equal to the 'in' input (the output remains in floating point per-channel, i.e. the same type as the input).
MaterialX Fract math node: Computes the fractional part of the float-based 'in' input.
MaterialX Ln math node: Computes the natural logarithm of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Multiply math node: Multiplies the 'in1' input by the 'in2' input. Vector/Color types multiply component-wise, while matrices use a standard matrix product.
MaterialX Max math node: Selects the maximum of the 'in1' and 'in2' inputs.
MaterialX Min math node: Selects the minimum of the 'in1' and 'in2' inputs.
MaterialX Modulo math node: Computes remaining fraction after dividing the 'in1' input by the 'in2' input and subtracting the integer portion. Modulo always returns a non-negative result.
MaterialX Power math node: Raises the 'in1' input to the exponent of the 'in2' input.
MaterialX Safe Power math node: Raises the 'in1' input to the exponent of the 'in2' input. When 'in1' is negative the output will also be negative.
MaterialX Sign math node: Outputs the per-channel sign of the 'in' input: -1 for negative, +1 for positive, or 0 for zero.
MaterialX Sin math node: Computes the sine of the angle in radians of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Sqrt math node: Computes the square root of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Subtract math node: Subtract the 'in2' input from the 'in1' input.
MaterialX Round math node: Rounds each channel of the 'in' input the nearest integer value.
MaterialX Tan math node: Computes the tangent of the angle in radians of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Transpose math node: Transposes the matrix of the 'in' input.
MaterialX Triangle Wave math node: Generate a triangle wave from the 'in' input, ranging from zero to one and repeating on integer boundaries.
MaterialX Invert Matrix math node: Inverts the matrix of the 'in' input. If the input matrix is not invertible, the output matrix will consist of all floating-point 'NaN' values.
MaterialX Determinant math node: Computes the determinant of the matrix of the 'in' input.
MaterialX ATan2 math node: The angle in radians from the X-axis to the line joining the origin and the point of 'inx' and 'iny' inputs.
MaterialX Clamp math node: Clamps the 'in' input to the range of ['low', 'high'].
MaterialX Cross Product vector math node: Computes the cross product of the 3D vector of the 'in1' input with the 3D vector of the 'in2' input.
MaterialX Dot Product vector math node: Computes the scalar float output of the vector dot product of the 2 vectors of 'in1' and 'in2' inputs.
MaterialX Create Matrix math node: Combines the 4 vector inputs of 'in1', 'in2', 'in3' and 'in4' into a matrix.
MaterialX Create 3x3 Matrix math node: Combines the 3 vector inputs of 'in1', 'in2' and 'in3' into a 3x3 matrix.
MaterialX Distance vector math node: Measures the distance between two points of 'in1' and 'in2' inputs in 2D, 3D, or 4D.

MaterialX Height To Normal vector math node: Convert a scalar height map to a tangent-space normal map (outputting 3D vectors). The output normal map is encoded with all channels in the [0-1] range, enabling its storage in unsigned image formats.

MaterialX Magnitude vector math node: Computes the float magnitude (vector length) of the vector of the 'in' input. Note: the fourth channel in vector4 input is not treated any differently, e.g. not as a homogeneous 'w' value.

MaterialX Normalize vector math node: Computes the normalized vector (of length 1) from the vector of the 'in' input. Note: the fourth channel in vector4 input is not treated any differently, e.g. not as a homogeneous 'w' value.".

MaterialX Normal-Map vector math node: Transforms a normal vector of input 'in' from the encoded tangent space to world space. The input normal vector is assumed to be encoded with all channels in the [0-1] range, as would commonly be output from a normal map. The transformation accounts for the basis vectors of the shading 'normal', 'tangent' and 'bitangent' inputs (assumed to be in world space).
MaterialX Reflect vector math node: Reflects the 3D incident vector of the 'in' input about the surface normal vector of the 'normal' input.

MaterialX Refract vector math node: Refracts the 3D incident vector of the 'in' input through a surface with the surface normal unit vector of the 'normal' input and relative index of refraction of the 'ior' input.
MaterialX Rotate 2D vector math node: Rotates the 2D vector of the 'in' input in 2D space about the origin by the angle in degrees of the 'amount' input.
MaterialX Rotate 3D vector math node: Rotates the 3D vector of the 'in' input in 3D space, about the 3D unit vector of the 'axis' input, by the angle in degrees of the 'amount' input.
MaterialX Transform Vector math node: Transforms the 3D vector of the 'in' input in 3D space, from the space of the 'fromspace' input to space of the 'tospace' input.
MaterialX Transform Normal math node: Transforms the 3D vector unit normal of the 'in' input in 3D space, from the space of the 'fromspace' input to space of the 'tospace' input.
MaterialX Transform Point math node: Transforms the 3D point of the 'in' input in 3D space, from the space of the 'fromspace' input to space of the 'tospace' input.
MaterialX Transform Matrix math node: Transforms the vector of the 'in' input by the 4x4 matrix of the 'mat' input.
MaterialX Transform 3x3 Matrix math node: Transforms the vector of the 'in' input by the 3x3 matrix of the 'mat' input.

MaterialX Geom Prop Value geometry node: Outputs the value of the specified varying geometric property (i.e: vertex attribute) specified by the 'geomprop' input, of the geometry bound to the material (selected node texture value type must match that of the referenced geomprop).
MaterialX Geom Color geometry node: Outputs the color at the shaded position (computed from vertex color) of the geometry bound to the material.

MaterialX Bump geometry node: Computes a 3D unit normal vector by offsetting the surface world space position along its world space normal at the shaded point on the surface of the geometry bound to the material.
MaterialX Tex Coord geometry node: Outputs the 2D or 3D texture coordinates of the shaded point on the surface of the geometry bound to the material.
MaterialX Position geometry node: Outputs the 3D position of the shaded point on the surface of the geometry bound to the material, in the space of the 'space' input.
MaterialX Normal geometry node: Outputs the 3D unit normal vector of the shaded point on the surface of the geometry bound to the material, in the space of the 'space' input.
MaterialX Tangent geometry node: Outputs the 3D unit tangent vector of the shaded point on the surface of the geometry bound to the material, in the space of the 'space' input.
MaterialX BiTangent geometry node: Outputs the 3D unit bi-tangent vector of the shaded point on the surface of the geometry bound to the material, in the space of the 'space' input.

MaterialX Facing Ratio geometry node: Computes the geometric facing ratio (a [0-1] float value) as the dot product between the view direction of the 'viewdirection' input and geometric normal of the 'normal' input.
MaterialX Up Direction application node: Outputs the 3D vector pointing upwards, in the space of the 'space' input.
MaterialX View Direction application node: Outputs the 3D view direction vector (e.g. from the viewing/camera position to the current shading position), in the space of the 'space' input.
MaterialX Extract channels node: Isolate a single float channel from a 4D vector or an RGBA color with an alpha channel.
MaterialX Extract channels node: Isolate a single float channel from a 3D vector or an RGB color.
MaterialX Extract channels node: Isolate a single float channel from a 2D vector.
MaterialX Combine4 channels node: Combines 4 scalar float inputs into a single 4D vector or an RGBA color with an alpha channel.
MaterialX Combine3 channels node: Combines 3 scalar float inputs into a single 3D vector or an RGB color.
MaterialX Combine2 channels node: Combines 2 scalar floats into a 2D vector.
MaterialX Combine2 channels node: Combines 2 2D vectors into a 4D vector.
MaterialX Combine2 channels node: Combines a 2D vector and a scalar float into a 3D vector.
MaterialX Combine2 channels node: Combines a 3D vector and a scalar float into a 4D vector.
MaterialX Combine2 channels node: Combines an RGB color and a scalar float representing an alpha channel into an RGBA color.
MaterialX Convert channels node: Converts an input of any value type into an output of any other value type.
MaterialX Constant procedural node: Outputs a uniform (i.e: non-spatially varying) value.
MaterialX Ramp 4 procedural node: Generates a 4-corner bi-linear value ramp.
MaterialX Ramp Left Right procedural node: Generates a left-to-right linear value ramp.
MaterialX Ramp Top Bottom procedural node: Generates a top-to-bottom linear value ramp.
MaterialX Random Float procedural node: Generates a stable randomized float value between 'min' and 'max' inputs, based on an input signal of the 'in' input and optional 'seed' input value.

MaterialX Random Color procedural node: Generates a stable randomized RGB color value within a randomized hue, saturation and brightness ranges, based on an input signal of the 'in' input and optional 'seed' input value.
MaterialX Split Left Right procedural node: Generates a left-right split matte, split at a specified U value.
MaterialX Split Top Bottom procedural node: Generates a top-bottom split matte, split at a specified V value.
MaterialX Noise 2D procedural node: Generates a 2D Perlin noise in 1, 2, 3 or 4 channels.
MaterialX Noise 3D procedural node: Generates a 3D Perlin noise in 1, 2, 3 or 4 channels.

MaterialX Fractal 2D procedural node: Generates a zero-centered 2D Fractal noise in 1, 2, 3 or 4 channels, created by summing several octaves of 2D Perlin noise, increasing the frequency and decreasing the amplitude at each octave.

MaterialX Fractal 3D procedural node: Generates a zero-centered 3D Fractal noise in 1, 2, 3 or 4 channels, created by summing several octaves of 3D Perlin noise, increasing the frequency and decreasing the amplitude at each octave.

MaterialX Place 2D procedural node: Transforms 2D UV texture coordinates for 2D texture placement. The 'operationorder' input controls the order in which transform operations are performed. The 'SRT' option performs -'pivot', 'scale', 'rotate', 'translate', +'pivot'. The 'TRS' option performs -'pivot', 'translate', 'rotate', 'scale', +'pivot'.
MaterialX Cell Noise 2D procedural node: Generates a 2D cellular noise.
MaterialX Cell Noise 3D procedural node: Generates a 3D cellular noise.
MaterialX Worley Noise 2D procedural node: Generates a 2D Worley noise, using centered jitter, outputting a scalar float or 2D or 3D vectors (distance metric to closest 1, 2 or 3 features).
MaterialX Worley Noise 3D procedural node: Generates a 3D Worley noise, using centered jitter, outputting a scalar float or 2D or 3D vectors (distance metric to closest 1, 2 or 3 features).

MaterialX Tri Planar Projection procedural node: Samples data from three images and projects a tiled representation of the images along each of the three respective coordinate axes, computing a weighted blend of the three samples using the geometric normal.
MaterialX Time application node: Outputs the current time in seconds.
MaterialX Frame application node: Outputs the current frame.
OCIO view to use when displaying in the render viewport. This should be set to a view that produces output in sRGB.
Enable legacy behavior for Gaussian splats which makes them slightly transparent
Material metalness at the camera ray's hit point.
